prompt: Two sides of a triangular brace measure $7$ ft and $12$ ft. If the third side must be a whole number of feet, how many different lengths are possible?
hint: The third side has both an upper and a lower limit.

hints.text: The third side has both an upper and a lower limit.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try tiny numbers: with sides $2$ and $3$, the third side satisfies $1 < s < 5$, so $s$ is $2$, $3$ or $4$ — that is $4 - 2 + 1 = 3$ values. Build the range and count the same way with $7$ and $12$.
It must be less than $12 + 7 = 19$ and greater than $12 - 7 = 5$.
Whole numbers strictly between 5 and 19 run from 6 to 18, which is $18 - 6 + 1 = 13$ values.

explanation: The Triangle Inequality gives a range: the third side $s$ satisfies $12 - 7 < s < 12 + 7$, so $5 < s < 19$.
Both endpoints are excluded — at exactly 5 or exactly 19 the triangle flattens into a line.
The whole numbers that fit are $6, 7, 8, \dots, 18$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the ends carefully
steps: Counting a run of whole numbers means subtracting and then adding 1, because both ends are included in the run.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap answer is 14, from forgetting the "add 1 at the end" rule or from sneaking 5 or 19 into the list.

Remember the inequality is strict: a side of exactly 19 ft would lie flat along the other two, and a side of exactly 5 ft would too. Neither makes a triangle, so the count runs 6 through 18: 13 lengths.
